traits.note: Munger 2008, FEIS Cladonia (Cladina) spp. (read 2026-11-08): dense mats of richly branched podetia 4-12 cm tall and 0.6-1.8 mm wide; growth 5.0, 5.3 and 5.4 mm a year (C. stellaris, rangiferina, arbuscula, Seward Peninsula) and 3.9-5.9 in northern Russia; no cups. Typical height 6 cm: C. portentosa, the Puget prairies' reindeer lichen (Calabria et al. 2016), forms mats up to 6 cm tall, and drier sites grow podetia 4-6 cm (Wikipedia, Cladonia portentosa and C. rangiferina).

traits.podetium_tips.note: British Lichen Society species accounts (Cladonia portentosa, C. rangiferina, C. arbuscula, C. ciliata; read through a web search 2026-11-08): the terminal branches of C. rangiferina, C. arbuscula and C. ciliata are recurved and turned in one direction, C. ciliata's extreme tips curling down; C. portentosa's stand mostly erect in broccoli-like tufts, any recurved tips not turned one way. The Puget prairies hold C. ciliata, C. portentosa subsp. pacifica and C. rangiferina together (Calabria et al. 2016), so the subgenus takes recurved tips turned every which way.

traits.podetium_forks.note: C. portentosa: each branch usually divides into three, the penultimate sometimes into two; C. rangiferina into three or four, sometimes two; Cladina ramify once a year, as an anisotomic trichotomy or isotomic tetrachotomy (Wikipedia, Cladonia portentosa, Cladonia rangiferina, Podetium, read 2026-11-08).

traits.podetium_fork_angle_deg.note: No source measures it; C. portentosa branches at a wider angle than C. rangiferina (Wikipedia). Estimate from photographs; to measure.

traits.podetium_width_m.note: Thicker branches typically 1-1.5 mm (C. rangiferina, Wikipedia, read 2026-11-08); 0.6-1.8 mm over the group (FEIS).

traits.podetium_colour.note: Greyish, whitish or brownish grey (Wikipedia, C. rangiferina); the prairie form C. portentosa subsp. pacifica f. decolorans lacks usnic acid (Calabria et al. 2016) and is grey-white. Colour measured: the median, over 12 research-grade iNaturalist photographs of C. portentosa (imagekit batch inat-2026-11-08), of each photo's pale, unsaturated pixels (saturation under 0.2, value over 0.45, the lichen; 25-72% of each photo) at their 80th percentile by brightness: the lit faces of the branches, since a render adds the shade between them itself (their medians, shade included, 166-168-158). An overcast photograph of the Mima Mounds mat (Chris Light 2023, Wikimedia Commons) gives a bluer 195-200-202. Photographs' exposure, not a reflectance: to check against Kuusinen et al. 2020 (Remote Sensing of Environment 247: 111955), where C. stellaris and C. arbuscula reflect most of the boreal ground lichens in the visible.

traits.colony_spread_m_per_year.note: A mat's edge moves out by its fragments, most within 20 cm, at most 35-68 cm by wind (FEIS); taken as one year's growth of its tips, about 5 mm.
